newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang heads home after HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang heads home after HK handover.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin left Hong Kong by air for Beijing on Tuesday after ceremonies that returned the former British colony to China.
He was accompanied by Premier Li Peng, concluding their first-ever visit to this capitalist bastion, since midnight a Special Administrative Region of China, after 156 years of British colonial rule.

Jiang proclaimed a new era for Hong Kong as an autonomous part of China at a midnight ceremony when British royal heir Prince Charles handed the territory's 6.4 million people and trading bounty to the communist giant.
He later pledged that this international economic metropolis will "forever be vigorous and dynamic" under Beijing rule.
He told residents that a promised high degree of self-rule would be honoured for Hong Kong, now the richest city in China.

"The overwhelming majority of the laws previously in force will be maintained," Jiang said. "Hong Kong residents will enjoy their rights and freedoms in accordance with law and all will be equal before the law." China would retain Hong Kong's role as an economic powerhouse for East Asia.
